name: Laser iris depigmentation (Stroma laser)
lead: Laser iris depigmentation is a procedure, promoted for cosmetic eye color change, in which a laser is directed at the iris to reduce its melanin pigment and lighten the eye, typically from brown toward a lighter shade. It is discussed in hardmaxxing communities as a way to change eye color without an implant.

A Grokipedia summary of eye color change methods lists risks of laser depigmentation including raised intraocular pressure, glaucoma, cataracts and unpredictable color results, and states that the US FDA has not approved it for cosmetic use [1]. Eye color is described as determined by iris melanin, which is why pigment-targeting methods have been proposed [2][3].
No clinical trials of the cosmetic procedure were found among the sources reviewed.
infobox: Raised eye pressure, glaucoma, cataract, uneven color [1]
Not FDA approved for cosmetic use per summary [1]

paras: Proponents describe the procedure as targeting pigment in the front layer of the iris so that lighter tissue underneath shows. Technical details are not given here.

Iris melanin has been characterized in studies of irises with different colors [3]. Drug-induced changes in iris pigmentation, for example with latanoprost, have been studied as a function of eye color [4]. These studies concern other contexts and do not test laser depigmentation.

Reference summaries list glaucoma and cataract as risks of cosmetic laser depigmentation and state it lacks FDA approval for cosmetic use [1]. Wikipedia notes that ophthalmologists criticize cosmetic changes to healthy eyes because of the potential for vision loss [5].
No studies found. Studies of iris pigment and of drug-induced iris color change exist [3][4] but do not test laser depigmentation.

card.note: Reference summaries list glaucoma, cataract and unpredictable color results as risks.

quick.overview:
Laser iris depigmentation aims to lighten eye color by using a laser to reduce pigment in the iris.

No clinical trials of the cosmetic procedure were found, and a reference summary states it is not FDA approved for cosmetic use.
quick.mechanism: Eye color is determined by iris melanin; the procedure is meant to remove some of that pigment so the eye looks lighter.
quick.risks: Listed risks include raised intraocular pressure, glaucoma, cataracts and unpredictable color outcomes. Ophthalmologists criticize cosmetic alteration of healthy eyes because of potential vision loss.
